text:
alyssa: heads-up — multiple customers started reporting p99 latency spikes around 02:10UTC. Observability shows p99 ~2.1s (baseline ~220ms). Seeing a flurry of GPU OOM and allocation-failure logs in eu-west-2a GPU pool.

mike: link to dashboard?

alyssa: https://app.redwood/obs/dashboards/p99-latency?range=2h — filter = pool:eu-west-2a. Example metrics: p50=28ms p95=430ms p99=2.1s. Error stream includes repeated: `cudaErrorOutOfMemory` and our runtime logs `kv_cache_size growth exceeded quota` for several models.

jordan: oncall saw increased retry/backoff which blew up tail. Any recent rollout?

ops-bot: deploy slowroll finished - 02:05UTC - runtime v12.3.1 (allocator changes).

liam: allocator changes? we shipped a patch to improve caching but it changed default retention. Could be holding more KV shards in GPU memory for longer.

mike: repro steps from support (customer A): 1) start long chat session with model-x-1 2) send many short prompts that keep KV cache warm 3) observe progressive p99 growth then OOM and heavy CPU-side retries.

alyssa: pasted relevant logs: ```
[2026-03-14T02:12:21Z] ERROR runtime.worker: cudaErrorOutOfMemory: failed to allocate 3.2 GiB
[2026-03-14T02:12:21Z] WARN runtime.kvcache: kv_cache_bytes=12.7GiB quota=12.0GiB (pool: eu-west-2a node-7)
[2026-03-14T02:12:21Z] INFO runtime.request: request_id=xyz retrying due to allocation failure
```

liam: kv_cache_bytes at 12.7GiB -> that explains fragmentation + inability to fulfill a new allocation. The allocator change in v12.3.1 increased max_shard_retention_ms default. I reverted locally and could reproduce reduced fragmentation.

jordan: what mitigations did we run in prod?

mike: rolled back rollout on 3 nodes (node-5,7,9) at 02:25 — p99 dropped to ~800ms but still above baseline. Also increased autoscale target by +20% which bought headroom.

alyssa: we temporarily lowered KV retention to 15m for the eu-west-2a pool via runtime config: `kv.retention_ms=900000` (was 3600000). Observed a secondary improvement to p99 ~380ms after propagation.

liam: long-term fixes we discussed: 1) tune TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF (use max_split_size_mb) to reduce internal fragmentation; 2) expose per-model kv_max_entries and cap continuous-batching for long-chat sessions; 3) add eviction policy based on working_set_bytes and last_access_time; 4) consider enabling cudaMallocAsync pool when available.

mike: can we add an alert for kv_cache_bytes / gpu_total_mem > 0.85? Right now we only alert on OOMs.

alyssa: opened monitoring ticket: MON-4821 to add kv cache ratio alert + synthetic to exercise long-chat flows.

support-bot: escalated case TK-9981 to eng-runtime and eng-ml — customers impacted: 3 (high).

jordan: immediate runbook snippets we used: ```
# quick mitigations
- set runtime param: kv.retention_ms=900000 for pool eu-west-2a
- roll restart suspect nodes: nodectl drain node-7 && nodectl restart-service runtime && nodectl uncordon node-7
- temporarily increase dedicated pool autoscale cap by 15%
```

liam: note on fragmentation: restarting the process defragments the CUDA allocator so rolling restart helps but is disruptive. Better to tune allocator params and limit long-lived KV per-request.

mike: action list (owners):
- liam: PR with allocator-safe defaults + docs for TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF (eta: today EOD)
- alyssa: keep kv.retention override + monitor p99 (eta: 1h)
- jordan: update runbook with kv eviction commands + add alert MON-4821 (eta: 2h)
- ops: review autoscale headroom for eu-west-2a (eta: 3h)

alyssa: customer communication: posted interim note to affected customers — letting them know we've applied config mitigations and working on root cause.

support-bot: TK-9981 updated with actions and ETA.

mike: follow-up: we also saw one model that accidentally set `max_seq_len=4096` even though production load never needs it; reducing to 2048 removed ~1.8GiB per-request KV in that path. Please add a lint for obvious misconfigs.

liam: agreed. I'll add a telemetry counter for per-request kv_bytes and a guard in runtime that refuses allocations above 50% of free GPU mem for single requests.

alyssa: tl;dr — immediate: kv retention reduced + node restarts + autoscale. Medium: allocator default tuning + per-model kv caps + alerts. Long: make KV eviction smarter and add safety limits to prevent single-request blowouts.

mike: thanks everyone. I'll keep this thread updated. If you see regression after changes please @mike and paste traceId. :thumbsup:
